6º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 3

Comparatives and superlatives

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Compare two things with comparatives: taller than, more expensive than
  • Say which is the top one in a group with superlatives: the tallest, the most expensive
  • Use the irregular forms good, bad and far
  • Compare people, animals and places in short texts

Para pensar

Un guepardo es más rápido que un caballo. Pero ¿cuál es el animal terrestre más rápido de todos? ¿Cómo dirías «más rápido que» y «el más rápido» en inglés?

Explicación

Comparing two or more

When we compare two things we use the comparative: «A horse is bigger than a dog». When we choose the number one in a group of three or more we use the superlative: «The elephant is the biggest of the three».

En castellano: el comparativo es «más… que» y el superlativo es «el más… de». En inglés, el adjetivo cambia: big → bigger → the biggest. Detrás del comparativo va than («que») y delante del superlativo va the.

Short adjectives: -er and -est

Adjectives with one syllable add -er and -est: tall → taller → the tallest; fast → faster → the fastest; old → older → the oldest; small → smaller → the smallest.

Spelling: ending in -e, add only -r / -st: nice → nicer → the nicest. Consonant + vowel + consonant, double the letter: big → bigger → the biggest; hot → hotter → the hottest; thin → thinner → the thinnest.

Adjectives ending in -y

Adjectives with two syllables that end in -y change the y to -ier and -iest: happy → happier → the happiest; funny → funnier → the funniest; easy → easier → the easiest; heavy → heavier → the heaviest.

Example: «My cat is lazier than my dog, but my hamster is the laziest pet in the house!». En castellano: es la misma regla de la y que en el pasado (study → studied): la y se convierte en i.

Long adjectives: more and the most

Long adjectives (two or more syllables, not ending in -y) don't change. We put more or the most before them: interesting → more interesting → the most interesting; expensive → more expensive → the most expensive; beautiful, dangerous, important, popular…

«A tiger is more dangerous than a cat». «The blue whale is the most amazing animal I know». Never mix the two forms: not «more bigger» or «the most fastest».

Irregular forms

Three very common adjectives are irregular: good → better → the best; bad → worse → the worst; far → further → the furthest.

«This pizza is better than the last one». «It was the best day of my life!». «Monday is the worst day of the week». En castellano: también en español son irregulares: bueno → mejor (no «más bueno»), malo → peor. Por eso en inglés nunca se dice «gooder» ni «the goodest».

Superlatives in sentences

After a superlative we often say the group with in (places, groups) or of (a number or time): «Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world», «Ana is the tallest girl in my class», «It's the coldest day of the year».

We can also use the present perfect phrase I've ever (que he… nunca): «It's the best book I've ever read». En castellano: «el mejor libro que he leído nunca».

As … as: the same

To say two things are equal (iguales) we use as + adjective + as: «My brother is as tall as my dad». In the negative, not as … as means «less»: «A bike isn't as fast as a car».

Compare these sentences, they mean the same: «A car is faster than a bike» = «A bike isn't as fast as a car». En castellano: «as… as» es «tan… como». El adjetivo va en su forma normal, sin -er.

Reading: world records

Read about animal records: «The biggest animal in the world is the blue whale. It is heavier than thirty elephants! The cheetah is the fastest land animal: it is faster than a car in the city. The giraffe is the tallest animal, and its tongue is longer than your arm. Tortoises are slower than most animals, but some live longer than people. Which animal do you think is the most interesting?»

Let's practise: class records

Make a class record book in groups. Measure and ask: «Who is the tallest?», «Who has the longest name?», «Who lives the furthest from school?». Write the results: «Pablo is the tallest. His name is shorter than Alejandro's».

Then compare two places you know: your town and a big city. «My town is smaller and quieter than Barcelona, but Barcelona is more exciting». Consejo: cuenta las sílabas del adjetivo antes de elegir -er o more.

Comparatives and superlatives

Ejercicios

  1. Write the comparative: cold, nice, big, happy.

  2. Write the superlative: small, funny, expensive, good.

  3. Complete: «A mouse is (small) ___ a cat.»

  4. Complete: «August is (hot) ___ month of the year.»

  5. Complete: «Football is (popular) ___ handball in Spain.»

  6. Correct: «My bike is more good than yours.»

  7. Rewrite with as … as: «Tom is 12. Ana is 12.» (old)

  8. Rewrite with not as … as: «A car is faster than a bike.»

  9. Translate: «Es el peor día de la semana.»

  10. Compare three animals in three sentences.

Practica

  1. The comparative of «tall» is…

    1. A) more tall
    2. B) taller
    3. C) tallest

  2. The superlative of «big» is…

    1. A) the bigest
    2. B) the most big
    3. C) the biggest

  3. The comparative of «easy» is…

    1. A) easier
    2. B) easyer
    3. C) more easy

  4. The superlative of «beautiful» is…

    1. A) the beautifulest
    2. B) the more beautiful
    3. C) the most beautiful

  5. The comparative of «good» is…

    1. A) gooder
    2. B) better
    3. C) best

  6. The superlative of «bad» is…

    1. A) the worst
    2. B) the baddest
    3. C) the worse

  7. «Spain is bigger ___ Portugal.»

    1. A) that
    2. B) than
    3. C) as

  8. «It's the longest river ___ Spain.»

    1. A) of
    2. B) than
    3. C) in

  9. «Tan rápido como» is…

    1. A) as fast as
    2. B) so fast than
    3. C) as faster as

  10. Which sentence is correct?

    1. A) He is funniest boy in class.
    2. B) He is the funniest boy in class.
    3. C) He is the most funny boy in class.

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Diferencia entre comparativo y superlativo; Cuándo se usa -er/-est y cuándo more/the most; Cuáles son los irregulares good, bad y far; Cómo se dice «tan… como» en inglés.

Resumen

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

-er thanComparativo de adjetivos cortos.
the -estSuperlativo de adjetivos cortos.
-ier / -iestAdjetivos en -y: happier, the happiest.
more / the mostAdjetivos largos.
better / the bestComparativo y superlativo de good.
worse / the worstComparativo y superlativo de bad.
in / ofthe tallest in the class · of the year.
as … asTan … como.

Soluciones

  1. B) Una sílaba: -er.
  2. C) Se dobla la g.
  3. A) -y → -ier.
  4. C) Adjetivo largo.
  5. B) Irregular.
  6. A) Irregular.
  7. B) Comparativo + than.
  8. C) Lugar: in.
  9. A) as … as.
  10. B) the + -iest.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. colder, nicer, bigger, happier.
  2. the smallest, the funniest, the most expensive, the best.
  3. smaller than.
  4. the hottest.
  5. more popular than.
  6. My bike is better than yours.
  7. Tom is as old as Ana.
  8. A bike isn't as fast as a car.
  9. It's the worst day of the week.
  10. Model answer: A dog is bigger than a cat. A horse is faster than a dog. The elephant is the heaviest of the three.
